content:
People with good memories may have noticed that the iPhone Duo bears some resemblance to a prototype device called the Microsoft Courier that appeared in 2009.

My headline is, of course, half in jest: Microsoft never put this prototype into mass production and even abandoned the project less than a year later. Still, looking back now, it's astonishing how similar the integrated user interface they envisioned back then is to today's designs...

As I mentioned in an earlier article, Apple has shown the world how to properly make a foldable smartphone, and the clever integration between hardware and software is precisely the key.

One of the examples I gave was dragging part of a photo from one side of the screen to another app on the other side, so seeing Microsoft demonstrate nearly the same function in their 2009 concept video is quite interesting.

Microsoft did carry on similar functions on some Surface products, but ironically, it took Apple to truly achieve the level of integration that the company had originally conceived. Check out the video below.
